solves: Blocks the page with a modal window, over the overlay/scrim veil, until the person finishes or cancels a short task, such as editing a record, filling in a short form or choosing an option.
use_when: A short task that needs an answer before going on: edit a record, fill in a short form, choose an option.
Choose the size by the content, as the width ceiling: sm for a choice or a short confirmation without a destructive action, md for a short form, lg for a table, a long list or a two-column form.
Turn on the lines with long content, such as a list or a table.
Use stacked actions on a narrow screen.
do_not_use_when: To confirm a destructive action, such as deleting or discarding: use nph-alert-dialog.
For a long flow: it goes to a page.
For a notice that asks for no answer: use a message on the page itself.
To open a dialog over another: finish or close the first one.

heading.constraint: The title, already localized by the consuming application: the task or the question. It is the h2 of the header and the accessible name of the dialog. Empty or only spaces draws nothing and emits console.error in development. The name heading avoids title, a global HTML attribute that would show the browser's own balloon over the dialog.

description.constraint: The support sentence below the title, already localized, which completes the name: it becomes the accessible description of the dialog. Empty draws no description.

size.constraint: The Figma size P, M and G: the width ceiling. The dialog hugs its content, from layout/dialog-min-width up to layout/dialog-sm, -md or -lg. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the ceiling by it. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

actions.constraint: The Figma actions property. inline: the footer buttons on the right, side by side, the primary last. stacked: below the md breakpoint (768), one button per line, the primary on top; at or above it, inline. inline never stacks. Reflects because the internal CSS selects by it. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

hide-close.constraint: Turns off the close button, which the Figma set has on by default. Turn it off only when the footer already offers the way out. Esc still closes the dialog. The property is hideClose.

close-label.constraint: The accessible name of the close button, already localized, such as Close. Required while the close button is shown: without it, the dialog draws without the button and emits console.error in development. The property is closeLabel.

header-separator.constraint: The header line of the Figma set: an nph-separator between the header and the content, at space/stack from each. Turn it on with long content. The property is headerSeparator.

footer-separator.constraint: The footer line of the Figma set: an nph-separator between the content and the footer, drawn only when the footer has buttons. Turn it on with long content. The property is footerSeparator.

open.constraint: The state, and the only way to open and close the dialog. The dialog sets it to false itself when the person closes it with Esc or with the close button. Setting it from code never fires the event.

slot.constraint: The content area of the Figma set: fields, text, a list or another composition. Its width sets the width of the dialog, up to the ceiling of the size. Empty, the area is not drawn, as with the content area turned off in Figma. It is the only part that scrolls.

footer.constraint: The footer of the Figma set: the nph-button actions, the solid secondary first and the primary or the danger last, as the consumer writes them. Empty, the footer is not drawn.

nph-close.constraint: Fired before the dialog closes when the person asks: Esc (detail.source escape) or the close button (detail.source close-button). It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and is cancelable: preventDefault keeps the dialog open. The browser may refuse to hold a repeated Esc with no new activation by the person; then the event is not cancelable and the dialog closes.

size.choose_when: sm for a choice or a short confirmation without a destructive action; md, the default, for a short form; lg for a table, a long list or a two-column form.
do_not_combine_with: sm with a destructive action: that is nph-alert-dialog.

actions.choose_when: inline is the default. stacked on a narrow screen: below the md breakpoint, one button per line at full width, the primary on top.

closed.changes_for_user: The dialog is not shown and the page answers.

open.changes_for_user: The window appears over the veil, entering on motion/enter-duration; the page behind it does not answer and does not scroll.

business_rules: The dialog is modal: the rest of the page is inert while it is open, and the page does not scroll.

On open, the focus goes to the first element with autofocus in the content or the footer; otherwise to the first focusable element of the content, then of the footer, then to the close button, then to the window itself. On close, it goes back to the element that had it.
Esc and the close button ask to close: the dialog fires nph-close and closes unless the event is canceled. A click on the veil does not close it.
Above layout/dialog-max-height only the content scrolls; the header and the footer stay.
While the content scrolls and holds nothing focusable, it is a region named by the title in the Tab order, so the keyboard reaches the scroll; it is not a candidate of the focus rule on open.
The width hugs the content between layout/dialog-min-width and the ceiling of the size; without the content area, the header text sets the width up to the ceiling.
ai_hints: Use nph-dialog for a short task that needs an answer before going on; a long flow goes to a page and a notice with no answer stays on the page.
Write the task or the question in heading: it is the name the screen reader reads.
Put the fields in the default slot and the nph-button actions in the footer slot, the solid secondary first and the primary last.
Use the solid secondary for Cancel, never outline: inside the dialog it paints color/secondary-on-dialog by itself.
Use the primary in loading while the action finishes, instead of closing or disabling it.
To confirm a destructive action, choose nph-alert-dialog.
Open and close it only through open, and listen to nph-close to know when the person closed it.

accessibility.semantics: A native dialog element opened as modal (role dialog, aria-modal), in the top layer; the rest of the page is inert. The title is an h2.
accessibility.accessible_name: The heading names the dialog through aria-labelledby and the description completes it through aria-describedby. The close button is named by close-label.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move between the elements of the dialog and never reach the page.
Esc asks to close the dialog; a tooltip open inside it takes the first Esc.
Enter and Space activate the buttons, as in nph-button.
A content area that scrolls with nothing focusable inside takes the focus with Tab; the arrows and Page Down scroll it.
accessibility.focus: On open, the focus moves into the dialog by the rule of the business rules; on close, it goes back to the element that had it. The visible focus is the one of nph-button and of each element of the content; the content area that takes the focus draws focus/ring inside its own box.
accessibility.contrast: Title and description pass 4.5:1 on color/dialog in both modes; the text of the footer buttons passes on their own background, the secondary on color/secondary-on-dialog.
accessibility.color_alternative: The title says the subject and the buttons say the actions; color only reinforces.

invalid_combinations: An empty heading: the dialog has no name, so nothing is drawn.
A size other than sm, md or lg, or actions other than inline or stacked: nothing is drawn.
The close button on without close-label: the button would have no name, so it is not drawn.
A dialog opened over another: it opens and warns in development; finish or close the first one.
An outline secondary in the footer: the system default is the solid secondary.
anti_patterns: Using the dialog for a long flow, which belongs to a page.
Using the dialog for a notice that asks for no answer.
Using the outline secondary in the footer.
Confirming a destructive action with nph-dialog instead of nph-alert-dialog.
Turning off the close button when the footer offers no way out.
